summary: The root "rbH" primarily refers to a male ape or a young ape. It can also denote apes collectively.
lane: رُبَّاحٌ ذ (A' Obeyd, S, A, L, K) and , (A, TA,) the latter of the dial. of El-Yemen, (TA,) and , (L, TA,) The male ape; (S, A, L, K;) [ simia caudata, clunibus nudis: (Forskål, "Descr. Animalium" &c., p. iii.:)] or the young one of an ape: (TA:) or apes [as a coll. gen. n.]: (TA in art. نصح , in explanation of the last, which is there said to be originally رُبَاحٌ :) pl. of the first رَبَابِيحُ . (TA.) One says أَمْلَحُ مِنْ رُبَّاحٍ and رُبَاحٍ , meaning [ Prettier ] than the ape. (A, TA.) -b2- [Hence, app.,] رُبُّ رُبَّاحٍ (Lth, A, K) or رُبَاحٍ (A) A sort of dates (Lth, A, K) of ElBasrah. (Lth.) -b3- Also, (K,) accord. to some, (TA,) رُبَّاحٌ signifies A small young weaned camel, (K,) and small young camels, syn. حَاشِيَةٌ , (TA,) slender in the bones and meagre in the body: (K:) but A Heyth asks, How can it mean small young weaned camels, seeing that a poet applies to it the epithet ثَنِىّ , and the ثنىّ is five years old? and Khidásh Ibn-Zuheyr, in a verse cited by Sh, speaks of a ربّاح breathing hard in labour, in order that her young one might come forth. (TA.) -b4- See also رُبَحٌ .

headwords.def: رَبِحَ فِى تِجَارَتِهِر (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. رَبَحَ, (Msb, K,) inf. n. رِبْحٌ (Mgh, Msb, TA) and رَبَحٌ and رَبَاحٌ, (Msb, TA,) He gained; or made gain, or profit; in his traffic; (MA, KL, TK;) i. q. اِسْتَشَفَّ (S, K) or أَفْضَلَ. (Az, Msb.) The Arabs say to a man when he enters upon traffic, بِالرَّبَاحِ وَالسَّمَاحِ [ With gaining and liberality. ] (TA.) And رَبِحَتْ تِجَارَتُهُ (tropical:) (A, Msb, TA) His traffic brought him gain, or profit. (Msb, TA.)
: see 4. Also ربّح, inf. n. تَرْبِيحٌ, He took to himself ( اِتَّخَ َ ) an ape ( رُبَّاح, TA) in his place of abode. (K.)

أَعْطَاهُ مَالًا مُرَابَحَةً He gave him property on the condition that the gain, or profit, should be [ divided ] between them two. (TA.) And بِعْتُهُ المَتَاعَ مُرَابَحَةً (S, * Msb) I sold him the commodity naming a certain gain, or profit, for every portion of the price: (Msb:) you say, بِعْتُهُ السِّلْعَةَ مُرَابَحَةً عَلَى كُلِّ عَشَرَةِ دَرَاهِمَ دِرْهَمٌ [ I sold him the commodity on the condition of my receiving as gain, or profit, upon every ten dirhems, a dirhem ]: (TA:) and…

اربح فِى تِجَارَتِهِ He found a profitable market in [or for ] his traffic. (Az, Msb.) اربحهُ He gave him gain, or profit: (Mgh, Msb:) we have not heard; (Mgh;) [i. e.] رَبَّحْتُهُ as meaning I gave him gain, or profit, has not been transmitted [from the Arabs of classical times]. (Msb.) You say, أَرْبَحْتُهُ عَلَى سِلْعَتِهِ, (S,) or عَلَيْهَا, (A, K,) or both, (TA,) I gave him a gain, or profit, upon his commodity.
He sought gains, or profits. (A.) He (a man, TA) was, or became, confounded or perplexed, and unable to see his right course. (K.)

and and [all originally inf. ns.] Gain, or profit; (IAar, S, A, K, and Mgh in explanation of the first and last;) increase [ obtained ] in traffic; (TA;) excess, or surplus, [ obtained, ] above the capital [ expended ]; wherefore it is also termed شِفٌّ. (Ksh and Bd in explanation of the first in ii. 15.) [Hence,] البِرُّ خَيْرُ تِجَارَةٍ (tropical:) [ Piety is the best traffic in respect of gain, or profit. ] (A.)

: see the next preceding paragraph. Horses and camels that are brought from one place to another for sale. (K.) And Fat, as a subst. (S, K.) A poet says, (S,) namely, Khufáf Ibn-Nudbeh, (TA,) قَرَوْا أَضْيَافَهُمْ رَبَحًا بِبُحٍّ يعِيشُ بِفَضْلِهِنَّ الحَىُّ سُمْرِ [as though meaning They entertained their guests with fat, on the superabundant remains of which the tribe lived, by means of tawny-coloured gaming-arrows whereby the lots that determined who should afford the entertainment…

A young weaned camel; (S, K:) app. a dial. var. of رُبَعٌ. (S.) [See also رَبَحٌ and رُبَّاحٌ.] A lamb, or kid: (ISd, TA in art. نصح:) or the latter: (K;) as also. (IAar, K.) See also رُبَّاحٌ, first sentence. Also A certain bird, (S, K,) resembling the رَامِج [which is an owl employed for catching hawks]: or, accord. to Kr, the word is, and signifies a certain bird resembling the زَاغ [or rook ]. (TA.)

: see رِبْحٌ in two places. Also A certain small animal, resembling the cat. (So in many copies of the S.) F observes that J says, الرَّبَاحُ دُوَيْبَّةٌ يُجْلَبُ مِنْهَا الكَافُورُ; and that بَلَدٌ has been substituted as an amendment for دويبّة in some of the copies [of the S]; but that each of these readings is erroneous: for يجلب we find [in copies of the S] in the handwriting of Aboo-Zekereeyà and that of Aboo-Sahl يُحْلَبُ, with the unpointed ح; and the substitution of بلد for…

A certain kind of camphor: (K:) so called in relation to a certain country, or town, agreeably with what is [said to have been] asserted by J, or to a certain king named رَبَاحٌ, who applied his mind to this kind of camphor, and discovered it. (TA.)

(A' Obeyd, S, A, L, K) and, (A, TA,) the latter of the dial. of El-Yemen, (TA,) and, (L, TA,) The male ape; (S, A, L, K;) [ simia caudata, clunibus nudis: (Forskål, "Descr. Animalium" &c., p. iii.:)] or the young one of an ape: (TA:) or apes [as a coll. gen. n.]: (TA in art. نصح, in explanation of the last, which is there said to be originally رُبَاحٌ:) pl. of the first رَبَابِيحُ. (TA.) One says أَمْلَحُ مِنْ رُبَّاحٍ and رُبَاحٍ, meaning [ Prettier ] than the ape.

مَتْجَرٌ رَابِحٌ and (tropical:) Trafficking in which one makes gain, or profit; (TA;) and so تِجَارَةٌ رَابِحَةٌ; (T, S, A, * Msb, K;) [ lucrative, or profitable, traffic; ] a phrase like لَيْلٌ نَائِمٌ and سَاهِرٌ meaning "a night in which one sleeps" and "in which one is wakeful:" (Az, TA:) and بَيْعٌ a sale in which one makes gain, or profit.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
